validity.recommendation: Investigate whether P3948 ('Segment I', Uzen->Aktau, 149.10 km, 720mm, built 1974) is a legacy whole-route aggregate that double-counts the three granular segment rows P5776 (Kaz GPP-KS-Zhanaozen, 17.8 km, 720mm, built 1974) + P5777 (Zhanaozen-Zhetybay, 60.7 km, built 2008) + P5783 (Zhetybay-Aktau, 70.8 km, built 1968) -- those three sum to 149.30 km, within 0.20 km (0.13%) of P3948's own length, and P3948 exactly shares P5776's diameter (720mm) and start year (1974). If a human confirms P3948 is not an independently surveyed physical 'first string' distinct from the other rows, it should be merged/retired rather than left standing as a fourth, redundant whole-corridor entry -- do not delete unilaterally.
validity.researcher_notes: GEM's own roster shows five rows sharing this pipeline name: P3948 (Uzen->Aktau, 149.1 km, dia 720mm, cap 4.54, StartYear1 1974), P5776 (Kaz GPP->Uzen, 17.8 km, dia 720mm, cap 4.54, StartYear1 1974), P5777 (Uzen->Zhetybay, 60.7 km, dia 530mm, cap 4.54, StartYear1 2008), P5783 (Zhetybay->Aktau, 70.8 km, dia 529mm, cap 4.54, StartYear1 1968), and P5784 (Zhetybay->Kuryk branch, 70.0 km, cap 3.60 -- a separate spur, not part of this concern). 17.8+60.7+70.8 = 149.3 km, matching P3948's 149.10 km to within 0.13% -- far too precise to be a coincidental parallel-corridor match. P3948's diameter (720mm) and StartYear1 (1974) are identical to P5776's, not to P5777/P5783's (530/529mm, 2008/1968), which is the signature of a row that was built by copying one child segment's attributes and summing all children's lengths, rather than an independently surveyed pipe. Working against a clean 'duplicate, delete it' verdict: (1) P3948's own endpoints read Uzen->Aktau, which by GEM's own geography should exclude the Kaz GPP->Uzen leg (P5776) -- if P3948 really were the sum of all three, its endpoints should read Kaz GPP->Aktau, so the endpoint labeling is internally inconsistent with the apparent length-summing; (2) Intergas's own 2023 and 2024 annual reports (intergas.kz upload d8uwec4lky88goo8gks4.pdf, verified 200) explicitly describe a 2023 project 'Капитальный ремонт 3-х ниток МГ <<Жанаозен-Жетыбай-Актау>>' -- capital repair of THREE strings of the Zhanaozen-Zhetybay-Aktau trunk -- confirming the underlying trunk genuinely is a multi-string (3-string) system, so a distinct String I could legitimately exist in principle. The same annual report also lists 'МГ <<КазГПЗ-КС <<Жанаозен>>' (Kaz GPP-CS Zhanaozen) as a SEPARATELY NAMED pipeline from 'МГ <<Жанаозен-Жетыбай-Актау>>' in Intergas's own facility inventory under UMG Aktau -- i.e. Intergas itself does not treat the Kaz GPP-Zhanaozen leg (P5776) as 'Segment II' of the Zhanaozen-Zhetybay-Aktau system the way GEM's SegmentName field implies, which is a secondary attribution wrinkle worth a human look but not this row's primary problem. Net: the numeric match is too exact to ignore, but I could not find an independent source that names 'String I' specifically at 149.1 km, so I'm flagging this as a concern for human adjudication (merge candidate) rather than asserting it outright.

validity.recommendation: Re-verify Capacity=4.54 bcm/y. Two independent sources put this system's capacity at 3.60 bcm/y, not 4.54: a 2008 news article on the commissioning of the Uzen-Zhetybay reserve string (kt.kz) and the March-2019 Neft i Gaz technical journal's national trunk-pipeline table, which gives the whole 'Zhanaozen-Aktau' system as 3.6 bcm/y / 427 km. 3.60 is also exactly what P5784 (the Zhetybay-Kuryk branch) already carries in GEM, while P3948/P5776/P5777/P5783 all carry 4.54 identically. Confirm whether 4.54 reflects a genuine post-2019 upgrade (plausible given the 2023 capital-repair project on the 3 strings) or was propagated across rows without independent verification; do not treat 4.54 as confirmed until a current-dated source is found.
validity.researcher_notes: kt.kz (2008-12-24, 'В Мангистауской области <<КазТрансГаз Аймак>> ввел в эксплуатацию резервную нитку газопровода Жетыбай - Узень стоимостью более $30 млн', verified 200): reports the ~60 km Zhetybay-Uzen reserve string (matching P5777's route) commissioned at 3.6 bcm/y capacity, operator KazTransGaz Aymak, cost over $30M, financed by the Development Bank of Kazakhstan, built in 6 months. Neft i Gaz journal (March 2019, 'СОСТОЯНИЕ И ПЕРСПЕКТИВЫ РАЗВИТИЯ ТРАНСПОРТА НЕФТИ И ГАЗА КАЗАХСТАНА', http://neft-gas.kz/f/zhd_osmanov_pv_klimov.pdf, verified 200, this is citation #3 on the sheet's own gem.wiki page): lists Kazakhstan's major trunk gas pipelines with a table entry '5. <<Жанаозен-Актау>> - пропускная способность 3,6 млрд м3/год, протяженность 427 км (оператор АО <<КТГ-Аймак>>)' -- i.e. capacity 3.6 bcm/y, length 427 km, operator KTG-Aymak (KazTransGaz Aymak), for the system as a whole. Neither the 427 km figure nor the 3.6 bcm/y figure matches any individual GEM row cleanly (149.3 km is the P3948-family sum computed above; 368.4 km is the 5-row grand total including the Kuryk branch -- both well short of 427 km), so I am not proposing 427 km as a replacement value, only flagging that GEM's total system picture (whichever way it's summed) falls ~60-280 km short of this independent system-level figure and that 4.54 bcm/y has no independent corroboration I could find anywhere outside GEM's own rows. I deliberately did NOT stage these two sources as proposed_refs supporting GEM's existing 4.54/149.10 values, since they disagree with GEM rather than confirm it -- per standing rule, disagreement routes to a concern, not a silent pass.

fills.researcher_notes: Intergas's 2023/2024 annual report (verified 200) describes an active 2023 capital-repair project on the pipeline's 3 strings ('Капитальный ремонт 3-х ниток МГ <<Жанаозен-Жетыбай-Актау>>' and 'МГ <<КазГПЗ-КС Жанаозен>>') and lists the trunk under UMG Aktau's live facility inventory, confirming operating status. The March-2019 Neft i Gaz journal (verified 200) independently lists 'Жанаозен-Актау' among Kazakhstan's currently operating trunk gas pipelines with its own capacity/length figures. Two independent publishers, both confirming operating status as of 2019 and 2023-24.
Both sources refer to the line throughout as 'магистральный газопровод' (trunk gas pipeline) -- a gas pipeline, not oil/NGL. Trivial but independently corroborated by two separate publishers.

Both sources classify the line as a 'магистральный газопровод' -- i.e. a trunk/transmission gas pipeline operated by the national gas-transport operator (Intergas Central Asia / KazTransGaz Aymak), not a gathering or process line.

Single source (kt.kz 2008) names Uzen (Zhetybay-Uzen reserve line) as the field-side endpoint of this pipeline family, consistent with GEM's FuelSource='Uzen'. Only one independent article found naming Uzen specifically in this role, so tier=medium, not high.

Intergas's annual report places the Zhanaozen-Zhetybay-Aktau trunk under UMG Aktau (Mangistau region) alongside the other Aktau-branch lines. kt.kz (2008) independently ties the Zhetybay-Uzen leg to Mangistau region gas supply. Both corroborate Uzen->Aktau within Mangistau province.

Neft i Gaz journal (2019) names the 'Zhanaozen-Aktau' system's operator as 'АО <<КТГ-Аймак>>' (KazTransGaz Aymak JSC, abbreviated). kt.kz (2008) independently reports KazTransGaz Aymak commissioning the Zhetybay-Uzen reserve line. Two independent sources, both matching GEM's Operator value exactly.

summary: P3948 flagged with two concerns: (1) duplicate/aggregation -- its 149.10 km matches P5776+P5777+P5783's summed 149.3 km to within 0.13% and it shares P5776's diameter+start-year exactly, suggesting a legacy whole-route row double-counting the granular segments (human merge review recommended, not unilaterally deleted); (2) spec -- Capacity=4.54 bcm/y conflicts with two independent sources (kt.kz 2008, Neft i Gaz journal 2019) both giving 3.60 bcm/y for this system, which is what P5784 already carries. Staged verified REFS_ADDED refs for Status/Fuel/PipelineType/FuelSource/Location/Operator (all independently corroborated, values unchanged); Length, Diameter, StartYear1, and Capacity remain UNRESOLVED/unfilled pending the duplicate and spec concerns being adjudicated.
